## The Job

When a lab computer starts up, it could greet whoever sits down with a banner: a title in a box, then the facts about that computer. Write the program that prints it.

Here's one example. Your title, box style, and facts can be different.

```text
+==============================+
|        SYSTEM BANNER         |
|   Computer Science Lab 214   |
+==============================+

Name:   LAB-PC-14
System: Windows 11
CPU:    AMD64
Python: 3.13.1
Banner printed... done
```

## Your Program Must

1. Start with a comment giving your name, the date, and what the program does.
2. Print a **box around a title**, drawn with characters such as `+`, `-`, `=`, `|`, or `*`. The box has at least three lines, and **every line of the box is exactly the same width**.
3. Print a blank line between the box and the facts.
4. Print **at least four facts** about the computer, from four `platform` functions. Store each answer in a variable first, and give each fact a label.
5. Line up the facts, so the values start in the same column.
6. Use `sep` at least once, `end` at least once, and `\t` or `\n` at least once.

## Plan It First

Draw your box on graph paper or in your tracing notebook, **one character per square**. Count the characters on each line before you type it. Off-by-one spacing is the most common mistake.

Labels that are 7 characters or shorter line up with one `\t`. Longer ones jump to the next tab stop. Keep your labels short, or test what happens.

## Why the Facts Go Under the Box

The computer's name is a different length on every computer, so it would push the right side of a box out of line. In Lesson 4 you'll learn f-strings, which can pad a value to an exact width. Then you'll come back and put the facts *inside* the box.

## Check Before You Hand In

- [ ] It runs on the classroom computer with no errors.
- [ ] Every line of the box is the same width. (Hold a ruler to the screen, or count.)
- [ ] Four facts, each stored in a variable, each with a label, lined up.
- [ ] `sep`, `end`, and `\t` or `\n` each used at least once.
- [ ] Header comment at the top.
- [ ] Output pasted as a comment at the bottom of the file.

## Success Criteria

| | Level 1–2 | Level 3 | Level 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Application** | Runs, but the box is uneven or there are fewer than four facts | Even box, four labelled facts stored in variables, `sep`, `end`, and an escape character used | Also neatly lined up, with a design that would look at home on a real computer |
| **Communication** | Missing header comment or unclear labels | Header comment; clear labels and variable names | Clear, consistent names, labels, and comments throughout |
